questions.q: What does a 401 Unauthorized response typically indicate, as opposed to a 400 Bad Request?
options: A missing required field in the request body
An unsupported HTTP method
A closed accounting period
The request's credentials are missing, invalid, or expired — an authentication problem, not a content problem
questions.explain: 401 points to an authentication issue (bad or expired credentials/token), while 400 means the request reached the server but was rejected for a content reason.

questions.q: Why is reading the actual response body important, beyond just noting the status code?
options: It isn't important — the status code alone is always sufficient
The response body typically specifies the exact reason for a 400 error, such as which required field is missing
The response body always contains the fix automatically
The response body only matters for 401 errors
questions.explain: In this ticket, the response body specifically named the missing required field (BusinessUnit), which the status code alone would not reveal.

questions.q: What was the actual root cause of the sudden 400 errors on the Invoices REST resource?
options: The integration team changed their authentication token
The accounting period was closed
A quarterly Oracle Fusion update changed the resource so BusinessUnit became a required field on the request, where it had previously defaulted server-side
The middleware lost network connectivity
questions.explain: An Oracle-side update changed the resource's required-field behavior, which is why the integration team's own code appeared unchanged yet started failing.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a resource's 'describe' metadata (e.g., with metadataMode=minimal)?
options: To show exactly which fields are actually mandatory for a given resource, rather than relying on the full, broader schema
To show the full theoretical schema, which overstates what's actually required
To format payment files
To list invoice holds
questions.explain: The describe metadata (especially in minimal mode) clarifies which fields are genuinely required, since the full schema typically lists far more fields than are actually mandatory.

questions.q: Why does the resolution note recommend reviewing Oracle's quarterly update readiness notes going forward?
options: Because Oracle requires it contractually
Because quarterly updates always break every integration
Because it eliminates the need for authentication
Because this kind of REST resource behavior change can originate entirely from Oracle's side, and proactively reviewing update notes can catch it before an integration breaks in production
questions.explain: Since the root cause was a change Oracle made, proactively reviewing update notes before each update window could catch resource behavior changes before they cause a production failure.
